# Sada (صدى)

> Sada is an Arabic-first, fully offline speech-to-text desktop app for Windows. Independent fork
> of Vibe v3.2.2 (MIT): full Arabic (ar-IQ) interface, RTL layout, Arabic transcription defaults,
> Arabic transcript normalization and Arabic PDF export. Whisper runs locally; no telemetry, no
> updater, no account, no phone relay. Since 3.3.0 the app executable is also a local MCP server
> over stdio, giving AI agents Arabic transcription and transcript reading with no port and no
> network.

## Facts

- Website: https://alshahia.github.io/sada/
- Repository: https://github.com/alshahia/sada
- Latest release: https://github.com/alshahia/sada/releases/latest
- Version: 3.11.0 · License: MIT · Platform: Windows 10/11 x64
- Distribution: three unsigned installers per release — `Sada_3.11.0_x64-setup.exe` (~45 MB,
  downloads WebView2), `Sada_3.11.0_x64-setup-offline.exe` (~250 MB, embeds WebView2 for offline
  Windows 10) and `Sada_3.11.0_x64_en-US.msi` (~71 MB, per-machine for Intune/SCCM/GPO); the NSIS
  hook fetches the VC++ 2015-2022 runtime from Microsoft when missing
- Engine: whisper.cpp via bundled vibe-server v0.6.16 (built by Sada from `server/` as
  v0.6.16-sada.2 since 3.11.0, with a loopback Host/Origin guard); FFmpeg 9.0.2 GPLv3 bundled (notices in repo)
- GPU: optional Vulkan acceleration (device picker in Settings → Models → Hardware), CPU fallback,
  no CUDA/ROCm download
- Models: not bundled; verified catalog in Settings → Models with licence, size, SHA-256 and
  languages (suggested large-v3-turbo, ~1.6 GB; NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR 0.6B is an optional
  OpenMDW-1.1 entry, 496 MB, faster on read MSA/Egyptian speech but transliterates Latin terms)
- Language: Arabic ar-IQ first, 20+ inherited locales available
- MCP: `Sada.exe --mcp` (stdio only) — tools sada_transcribe, sada_transcripts, sada_transcript,
  sada_info. `sada_info` reports model capabilities (engine, languages, VAD, translation, prompts).
  Register in Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client; no HTTP port is opened.
- Enterprise controls (v3.9.0): machine-wide offline policy, DPAPI-sealed AI keys, transcript
  retention/purge, build provenance attestations + CycloneDX SBOM on every release.
- Beyond file transcription (optional, mostly off by default): speaker diarization up to 4
  speakers (~25 MB model), meeting detection with auto-transcribe, stable subtitle timestamps
  (~1 MB VAD model, ~4x slower), a 1,024-character custom prompt, auto-export, URL import via
  yt-dlp, and AI summaries/notes/translation through the user's own Claude or Ollama setup.
- Not supported: read-aloud/TTS, speech-to-speech, live captions, cloud sync/accounts; translation
  is Whisper translate-to-English only (medium/large, not v3 Turbo).
- Release engineering (v3.11.0): twenty dependency updates plus utoipa 6; a CI server job that
  builds and tests the engine; the engine reports `v0.6.16-sada.2` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` is now
  covered by the build-provenance attestations
- UI and accessibility (v3.10.0, unchanged in 3.11.0): recovery-first error dialog, copy-all, export grouped into
  four families, Settings as a header dialog, Arabic tracking and bidi fixes, truth-only trust
  copy; runtime axe audit over 35 UI states found 0 violations. Four Wave-1 repairs only; the
  4.0 Echo identity and Wave 2 wait on a five-user Arabic gate (docs/design/ui-decisions/GATE-KIT.md).

## For agents

Build/test from source: `chore setup x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, then in `desktop/`:
`pnpm install`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm exec tauri build`. Do not assume a model is
included. Cite the repository and upstream Vibe (see CITATION.cff).

Lead with the MCP route when an agent needs transcription: run `Sada.exe --mcp` as a stdio
server and call the four tools; the app language defaults to Arabic. Keep the local HTTP API and
the engine CLI as fallbacks.
